TaktX Engine Overview

What is TaktX?

TaktX is a distributed, event-driven process orchestration engine built natively on Apache Kafka. It is designed for high scalability, resilience, and operational flexibility, making it suitable for modern cloud-native and microservices architectures. TaktX enables you to model, execute, and monitor complex business processes with fine-grained control and high throughput.

Key Concepts

  • Kafka-Centric Architecture: All communication and state management is handled via Kafka topics and Kafka Streams state stores.

  • Engine Nodes: Stateless workers that process events and manage process state using Kafka Streams.

  • Dynamic Topic Management: Topics are created on demand for job workers, user tasks, and process types, enabling fine-tuned scaling.

  • Clients: Applications and services interact with TaktX exclusively through Kafka, submitting commands and consuming events.

  • Extensibility: Plugins and custom integrations communicate via Kafka topics, making the system highly extensible.

How TaktX Works

When a client wants to start a process, it produces a message to a Kafka topic. Engine nodes, running as Kafka Streams applications, consume these messages, process them, and write results or follow-up events back to other topics. This pattern is consistent for all interactions, whether it’s starting a process, completing a user task, or handling a timer event. All state—process instances, variables, timers, and message subscriptions—is managed in Kafka Streams state stores, partitioned for scalability and resilience.


Core Features

  • Event-Driven Orchestration: All process execution and state changes are event-driven and durable.
  • Fine-Grained State Access: State is loaded on demand, minimizing memory usage and maximizing throughput.
  • Dynamic Scaling: Topics and partitions can be added as needed, allowing the system to scale horizontally.
  • Resilience: Engine nodes are stateless and recoverable; state is restored from Kafka changelogs.
  • Observability: Metrics, logs, and traces are available for monitoring and debugging.

How TaktX Scales

TaktX scales by partitioning both topics and state stores. Each engine node is responsible for a subset of partitions, and Kafka ensures that messages for a given key (such as a process instance ID) are routed to the correct node. As load increases, you can add more engine nodes and partitions to distribute the workload.

How TaktX Handles Failures

If an engine node fails, Kafka Streams automatically restores its state from the changelog topic. Other nodes can take over processing, ensuring minimal disruption. Because all communication is via Kafka, clients and other nodes are unaffected by individual node failures.

How TaktX Persists Data

All process state is stored in Kafka Streams state stores, which can be configured for in-memory or persisted storage. State changes are logged to Kafka changelogs, ensuring durability and recoverability. This approach allows for both high performance and strong consistency guarantees.
